details.method: For model-authored designs consumed by a native parser, expose one canonical pending-confirmation template and validate it with that actual parser. Report specific structural errors instead of assuming normal prose will fit the hidden input contract. Pin the exact shared template bytes in the consumer UI trial, and distinguish parse/unit tests, dialog confirmation/cancel and business production. Inspect the actual fixture report, not only the wrapper process exit.
details.when: The editor generates a design document that the same editor consumes for dependency-based production.
details.counterexample: Human-only prose without a machine consumer does not need rigid headings; a parsed document still does not grant execution authority or replace explicit confirmation. A legacy FINALIZED fixture does not test the canonical template; a wrapper can return zero while its fixture report is failed. Dialogs need only expose their actual documented contract.
details.trial_plan: On the next same-domain change, plan and run an exact-template installed UI probe with pinned template/binary hashes, native pending/cancel checks and original malformed/stale checks; propagate runner exit and require both report.ok and editor.ok. Only then mark this revised method verified.
